title: WPMS/2940/2016 of Harendra Singh Rawat Vs Secretary Department Of Education Dehradun AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2940 of 2016
Harendra Singh Rawat .....Petitioner
Versus
Secretary Department of Education
Dehradun and others ....Respondents
Advocate : Mr. Navnish Negi, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand
Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, Advocate for respondent No. 5.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The petitioner, who claims himself to be an ex President of
the Committee of Management of Public Inter College, Devrajkhal,
District Pauri Garhwal, which is a grant-in-aid Institution governed by
the provisions of the Uttarakhand School Education Act, 2006, and the
same is managed and regulated under the Scheme of Administration, as
framed under Section 29 of the Uttarakhand School Education Act, 2006
and the said scheme of administration stands approved under Section 34
of the said Act.
2. On the expiry of the term of the Committee of Management,
as per clause 8 is three years, the grievance of the petitioner is that, prior
to election, certain ordinary members were inducted into the Society,
though they have deposited their membership fee on 01.03.2016 and
thereafter and hence they ought not to have been permitted to participate
in the election or cast their votes in the election in accordance with the
limitation which has been imposed by sub clause (1) Clause 4 of the
Scheme of Administration, which is quoted hereunder:-

3. But the fact, which has been born out from the writ petition
is that on the culmination of the term of the Committee of Management
an advertisement was issued as back as on 21.02.2016, and as a
consequent thereto, a newly elected body came into existence and it is in
the helm of affairs of the Committee of Management, who is managing
the affairs of the Institution as per the approved scheme of
Administration. After the election of the new Body, the same was placed
before the Chief Education Officer for its approval and the approval was
granted in favour of the newly elected Body, who is managing the
Institution of respondent No. 6.
4. Grievance of petitioner is that in the election of new body
held in 2016, even those members were permitted to vote in
contravention to clause 4 sub clause (1) of the Scheme of Administration,
who were inducted as new member for period of less than 6 months, and
had participate in the election. This permission granted to those members
to cast their vote would be arbitrary and violative of the Scheme of
Administration itself.
5. Questioning the approval granted, the petitioner had
preferred a writ petition before this Court being Writ Petition (M/S) No.
2861 of 2016, Harendra Singh Rawat v. Secretary Department of
Education & others, wherein the petitioner on the expiry of the term of
the Committee of Management dated 24.07.2016 had come up before this
Court against an advertisement issued on 21.02.2016, inviting the new
membership for the purposes of being inducted as members of the
Society. The said writ petition was disposed of on 18.10.2016 by the
coordinate Bench of this Court with an observation that the petitioner can
make a representation to the Chief Education Officer, who would
consider and decide the claim of the petitioner. The same reads as under:-
"3. Since the election process started, no interference is
being made in the ongoing election process. However, the
petitioner will be at liberty to move a representation before

3
the Chief Education Officer, Pauri Garhwal in this regard,
who shall take a decision on it, as expeditiously as possible."
6. The said order of 18.10.2016, had rather declined to
interfere, because after the issuance of the advertisement dated
21.02.2016, the election process of electing the new Committee of
Management was already initiated. The Chief Education Officer on being
served with the order/judgement dated 18.10.2016 rendered in Writ
Petition (M/S) No. 2861 of 2016, the Chief Education Officer had
considered the representation of the petitioner and had rejected the same
by virtue of the impugned order dated 22.10.2016 which is under
challenge in the present writ petition.
7. The Chief Education Officer, after considering the rival
contentions on the representation of the petitioner dated 20.10.2016 had
considered the impact of Clause 4(1) of the Scheme of Administration
and had rejected the representation for the following reasons :-

8. As a consequence thereto the effect would be that all those
members, who have deposited their membership fees, as shown in the list
to be of 01.06.2016 have been held out to be valid members who were
entitled to cast their vote in terms of Clause 4(1) of the Scheme of
Administration. As a result thereto, the representation of the petitioner
has been rejected. The rejection of petitioner's representation by the
Chief Education Officer would not take away the right of the petitioner to
approach the Prescribed Authority, as defined under the Societies
Registration Act, 1860, wherein under Section 25 as inserted by UP Act
No. 11 of 1984, it had provided a Forum, where the dispute pertaining to

4
the election of the Office Bearers of the Society could be redressed and
various other aspects as included therein could be opportunity dealt with
by the Prescribed Authority, the petitioner ought to have approached to
the Prescribed Authority for redressal of his grievance against the
election result or wrongful induction of members as it will also fall to be
within the nature of election dispute, as declaring the new Body of
Committee of Management which is elected to manage the affairs of the
College in question.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioner, in support of his
contention has placed reliance on a judgement rendered by the Hon'ble
Apex Court as reported in 1981 (1) SCC 722, Ajay Hasia and others v.
Khalid Mujib Sehravardi and others and in particular, the reference has
been made by the petitioner to contents of para 9 of the said judgement
which is quoted hereunder:-
"9. The tests for determining as to when a corporation can
be said to be a instrumentality or agency of Government
may now be called out from the judgment in the
International Airport Authority's case. These tests are not
conclusive or clinching, but they are merely indicative
indicia which have to be used with care and caution, because
while stressing the necessity of a wide meaning to be placed
on the expression "other authorities", it must be realised that
it should not be stretched so far as to bring in every
autonomous body which has some nexus with the
Government within the sweep of the expression. A wide
enlargement of the meaning must be tempered by a wise
limitation. We may summarise the relevant tests gathered
from the decision in the International Airport Authority's
case as follows:
(1) One thing is clear that if the entire share capital of the
corporation is held by Government it would go a long way
towards indicating that the corporation is an instrumentality
or agency of Government.
(2) Where the financial assistance of the State is so much as
to meet almost entire expenditure of the corporation, it
would afford some indication of the corporation being
impregnated with governmental character.

5
(3) It may also be a relevant factor...whether the corporation
enjoys monopoly status which is the State conferred or State
protected.
(4) Existence of deep and pervasive State control may afford
an indication that the Corporation is a State agency or
instrumentality.
(5) If the functions of the corporation of public importance
and closely related to governmental functions, it would be a
relevant factor in classifying the corporation as an
instrumentality or agency of Government.
(6) Specifically, if a department of Government is
transferred to a corporation, it would be a strong factor
supportive of this inference of the corporation being an
instrumentality or agency of Government.
If on a consideration of these relevant factors it is found that
the corporation is an instrumentality or agency of
government, it would, as pointed out in the International
Airport Authority's case, be an 'authority' and, therefore,
'State' within the meaning of the expression in Article 12."
10. The said judgement provides that where a Society which is
under an effective and pervasive control of the State, the alternative
remedy would not create a bar because under the Act, as it then existed, it
was held that tests were not held to be conclusive and clinching and
being an Autonomous Body having nexus with the Government, cannot
be left remediless and hence they could have approached to the Courts
available at that relevant point of time.
11. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is
not being accepted by this Court at the present moment for the reason
being that the controversy in the said judgement emanated from a dispute
which arose amongst the two rival society, claiming a right to manage the
Regional Engineering College, Srinagar, as well as for the purposes of
redressal of dispute of induction of its employees. However, the ratio, on
which the reliance has been placed by the learned counsel for petitioner
would not be relevant and applicable in the instant case, because after the
amendment made under the U.P. Act No. 11 of 1984, which was made
after the said judgement of 1981, the remedy, which would be available

6
to the petitioner would be to approach before the Prescribed Authority for
questioning the election of respondent No. 6 by invoking the provisions
of Section 25 of the Societies Registration Act.
12. Whereas, on the other hand, the learned counsel for the
respondent had placed reliance on a judgement rendered by the Division
Bench of this Court, as reported in 2011(1) U.D. 152, Jaipal Singh v.
State of Uttarakhand and others, wherein, in para 3 of the said
judgement it has been held out that wherever there happens to be dispute
pertaining to the election of a Body of a Society registered under the
Societies Registration Act, and particularly, when it happens to be in
relation to the election of the Committee of Management of an aided
institution and its approval given by Chief Education Officer the
mechanism has already been provided by the amendment made under
Section 25 of the Societies Registration Act, the petitioner would have
remedy available to him by approaching before the Prescribed Authority
by raising an election dispute. Para 3 of the said judgement is quoted
hereunder:-
"3. In the writ petition, order dated 11th June, 2010 passed
by the District Education Officer, Hardwar was impugned,
whereby and under, he granted approval to the election of
the office bearers of the committee of management. The
committee of management, thus elected, approval whereof
had been given by the order impugned in the writ petition, is
the committee also of the Society. Under the scheme of
management sanctioned for the institution in question, if
there are disputes pertaining to membership and posts, the
same can be sorted out by the President or the District
Education Officer and if the dispute is as to the claim by two
or more managing committees, the same may be sorted out
by the Divisional Educational Director on a reference to be
made by the District Education Officer. Further more, the
President or the District Education Officer has a right under
the scheme of administration to decide who will use the
rights related to the disputed post and who will perform the
work of the said post. In other words, as aforesaid, the
scheme of administration does not provide any mechanism
of sorting out election disputes, though the members of the
managing committee, the Manager and the President are to
be elected in terms of the mandate contained in the scheme

7
of administration. When the election of the managing
committee of the institution is election of office bearers of a
registered society and when a devise for sorting out disputes
pertaining thereto have been provided specifically in a
statute and the same has not been touched otherwise, the
corollary would be that a person seeking to challenge
election of such office bearers can do so only through the
mechanism provided in Section 25 of the said Act and not
otherwise. We, therefore, have no scope of interference."
13. In view of the reasoning given by the Division Bench's
judgement in para 3, this Court is of the view that as against the election
of respondent No. 6, or the issue pertaining to the wrongful induction of
the members and further permitting them to participate in the election,
which, according to the petitioner happens to be in contravention to the
provisions contained under Clause 4(1) of the Scheme of Administration
would be an issue, which will fall within the ambit of Section 25, which
has to be agitated by the petitioner before the Prescribed Authority under
Section 25 of the Act only.
14. Consequently, I don't find any merit in the writ petition, if
advised, petitioner can avail his remedy under Section 25 of the Societies
Registration Act, by challenging the election itself. Accordingly, the writ
petition is dismissed. However, there would be no order as to costs.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 22.04.2019
Mahinder/
